primary_meaning: Divine judgment and wrath (including eschatological punishment)

alternatives.meaning: Manifest presence or theophany of God (often as consuming holiness)
Purification, refining, or testing of people/works
Zeal, passion, or devouring intensity (e.g., prophetic word or divine service)

notes: Fire is polyvalent and context-dependent across the canon; Christian teaching and biblical studies routinely recognize multiple concurrent senses rather than one exclusive primary meaning. Judgment (especially hell/eschaton) receives heavy emphasis in moral and apocalyptic instruction, while presence, Spirit, and purification are equally standard in other loci. No single settled symbolic consensus overrides the others.
